title: Reversal on governing with Herbert Kickl's FPÖ (January–February 2025)
description: As ÖVP secretary-general, Stocker signed the party's first official statement in July 2023 calling FPÖ leader Herbert Kickl 'a security risk' and later declared that 'the People's Party will not lift a security risk into office' (profil). After the first ÖVP–SPÖ–NEOS talks failed and Karl Nehammer resigned, Stocker, named acting ÖVP chairman on 5 January 2025, said he would accept an invitation to talks if President Van der Bellen gave the FPÖ, the strongest party in the 2024 election, the mandate to form a government, which the party executive had authorised; ORF noted that the ÖVP had previously ruled such talks out and that Stocker had been among Kickl's sharpest critics. On 8 January 2025 he set conditions such as media freedom, independence from Russia and a constructive role in the EU. He acknowledged that the reversal put his credibility at risk, arguing that 'the country urgently needs a government' (ORF). The talks broke down on 12 February 2025, when Kickl returned the mandate; each side blamed the other, Kickl saying the ÖVP had insisted on keeping the interior and finance ministries (ORF).
key_facts: July 2023: as secretary-general, Stocker called Kickl a security risk for Austria (profil)
5 January 2025: Stocker became acting ÖVP chairman and said he would accept talks with the FPÖ (profil)
8 January 2025: ÖVP–FPÖ talks announced; Stocker set conditions on media freedom, Russia and the EU (ORF)
12 February 2025: Kickl returned the mandate to form a government; the President announced new consultations (ORF)
29 March 2025: at his election as party chairman Stocker said he was 'no partner for an Austria that becomes Trumpified' (ORF)

title: ÖVP criminal complaint against Climate Minister Leonore Gewessler (2024)
description: After Climate Minister Leonore Gewessler (Greens), then the ÖVP's coalition partner, voted for the EU Nature Restoration Regulation in June 2024 against the position of the ÖVP-led agriculture ministry and the federal states, the ÖVP, of which Stocker was secretary-general, filed a criminal complaint for abuse of office against her in the name of the federal party at the Vienna public prosecutor's office on 20 June 2024 and announced an annulment action before the EU Court of Justice. The Economic and Corruption Prosecutor's Office (WKStA), to which the complaint was passed, found no initial suspicion in early September 2024, describing her vote as 'an act of legislation' rather than an official act, and did not open proceedings. Stocker said the ÖVP took note of 'the conspicuously quick dismissal ... in the month before the National Council election' and maintained its legal view; the Greens demanded an apology. On 22 October 2024 the Chancellery decided not to file the annulment action because the required agreement of the ministries concerned could not be obtained.
key_facts: 20 June 2024: complaint under § 302 of the Criminal Code filed in the name of the ÖVP federal party (ORF)
September 2024: WKStA did not open proceedings for lack of initial suspicion (ORF)
13 September 2024: Stocker criticised the timing of the decision and upheld the party's legal view (ORF)
22 October 2024: no annulment action filed at the EU Court of Justice (ORF)

title: Wöginger case: Stocker's reaction to the diversion and the later first-instance conviction (2025–2026)
description: August Wöginger, chairman of the ÖVP parliamentary group, was tried at the Linz Regional Court on charges brought by the WKStA of incitement to abuse of office over the alleged arrangement of the post of head of the Braunau tax office for a party colleague; he denied wrongdoing. In October 2025 the court granted a diversion against a payment of €44,000 after he declared that he 'took responsibility', which was not a confession. Stocker publicly stressed his friendship with Wöginger and said: 'With that the matter is closed for him and for the People's Party' (quoted by profil). After criticism of the diversion, the Senior Public Prosecutor's Office in Vienna, with the approval of the Justice Ministry and its advisory council on instructions, instructed the WKStA to appeal against it, so that the Higher Regional Court in Linz had to review the diversion; the case then went to a trial lasting several weeks. In early May 2026 a lay-judge panel of the Linz Regional Court found Wöginger guilty of incitement to abuse of office, not with final effect, and sentenced him to seven months suspended and a fine of €43,200. Wöginger resigned as parliamentary group chairman but kept his seat; after Stocker's preferred successor declined, the ÖVP group elected Ernst Gödl, proposed by Stocker. The verdict is not final and Wöginger is presumed innocent. Stocker is not a party to these proceedings.
key_facts: October 2025: diversion against €44,000 at the Linz Regional Court; Stocker said the matter was 'closed' (profil)
30 October 2025: the Senior Public Prosecutor's Office in Vienna instructed the WKStA to appeal against the diversion (profil)
May 2026: first-instance conviction of Wöginger, not final: seven months suspended and a €43,200 fine (profil)
Ernst Gödl elected ÖVP parliamentary group chairman on Stocker's proposal (profil)
Wöginger, not Stocker, is the defendant; the conviction is not final and the presumption of innocence applies

title: Role in the election of the ORF director-general (2026)
description: Ahead of the Foundation Council's election of a new director-general of the public broadcaster ORF, profil reported in May 2026 that Stocker and ÖVP secretary-general Nico Marchetti had met almost all potential candidates and let it be known that the ÖVP favoured Clemens Pig, head of the APA news agency, before applications had been received or hearings held. profil wrote that this had caused 'great indignation' and that unsuccessful candidates or a federal state might take legal action, citing the transparency requirements of the European Media Freedom Act. In a session that ended in the early hours of 12 June 2026, the Foundation Council elected Pig with 21 of 35 votes; he takes office on 1 January 2027 (ORF).
key_facts: 31 May 2026: profil reported that the ÖVP signalled its preference for Clemens Pig before the formal procedure
12 June 2026: Pig elected ORF director-general with 21 of 35 votes after a session of more than 15 hours (ORF)

title: Remark that childcare is not unpaid work (August 2026)
description: At a citizens' forum in Salzburg during his summer tour on 6 August 2026, asked how he would support women, Stocker said: 'Childcare is for me not unpaid work ... I would not see it as work' (ORF). The remark was criticised by the FPÖ, the Greens, the coalition partners SPÖ and NEOS and the trade-union federation's women's chair; Vice-Chancellor Andreas Babler wrote that 'childcare is work'. The next day Stocker said in a statement that the sentence was 'wrong', apologised 'to all who feel hurt, insulted or not valued' and wrote that childcare is work, while maintaining that family is 'not a business case'. An alliance of women's organisations called a protest in front of the Chancellery, saying the apology was not sufficient.
key_facts: 6 August 2026: remark at a citizens' dialogue in Salzburg (ORF)
7 August 2026: Stocker called the sentence wrong and apologised (ORF)
Criticism from FPÖ, Greens, SPÖ and NEOS; support from Family Minister Claudia Bauer and Lower Austria's governor Johanna Mikl-Leitner (ÖVP)

title: Coalition disputes and failed FPÖ no-confidence motion (autumn 2026)
description: In September 2026 the SPÖ-led Finance Ministry said a 1 January 2027 start of Stocker's 'Zukunftsdepot' savings project was 'technically practically impossible' and not financed, and ÖVP minister Claudia Bauer accused Finance Minister Markus Marterbauer of 'ideological reservations' (Salzburg24/APA). On 14 October 2026 Marterbauer said he had promised the SPÖ's nine regional chairs to take over as Vice-Chancellor at the start of 2027 (trend/APA). On 15 October 2026 the FPÖ moved a motion of no confidence in the whole government in the National Council, with Kickl calling it 'the most expensive, most bloated, most incompetent and most unpopular government of all time'; only the FPÖ voted for it. Stocker was represented by State Secretary Alexander Pröll, who called the motion 'polemics' and listed the government's measures (trend/APA). On 17 October 2026 the coalition leaders announced agreements on the Zukunftsdepot, the university budget and a media package (BKA).
key_facts: 6 September 2026: public dispute between the Finance Ministry and the ÖVP over the Zukunftsdepot (Salzburg24/APA)
14 October 2026: Marterbauer confirmed he would become Vice-Chancellor at the start of 2027 (trend/APA)
15 October 2026: FPÖ no-confidence motion against the government failed; only the FPÖ voted in favour (trend/APA)
17 October 2026: 'autumn of results' agreements announced by Stocker, Babler and Meinl-Reisinger (BKA)

title: Testimony before the Pilnacek inquiry committee (October 2026)
description: The National Council's inquiry committee on the investigations into the death of Christian Pilnacek, the former head of the Justice Ministry's criminal-law section, was set up on 22 October 2025 at the FPÖ's request. On 8 July 2026, at the FPÖ's request, it summoned Stocker, his predecessor Karl Nehammer, former National Council president Wolfgang Sobotka, Interior Minister Gerhard Karner and Justice Minister Anna Sporrer, among others, as witnesses (Auskunftspersonen) for the autumn. On 21 October 2026 Stocker testified for about three hours. He said he had known Pilnacek from his time as a lawyer and later through Pilnacek's comments on legislative projects, and that he had not perceived any advisory services by Pilnacek for the ÖVP; according to a WKStA analysis of Pilnacek's laptop reported in the media, Pilnacek had informally advised ÖVP politicians including Sebastian Kurz. Stocker was asked about e-mails in which, as ÖVP secretary-general, he had exchanged views with Pilnacek on planned changes to anti-corruption criminal law and had written that he was trying 'to save what can be saved'; he described Pilnacek's input as legal remarks. After Green MP Nina Tomaselli spoke of a lack of awareness of wrongdoing, Stocker said he would 'not accept this' and would examine the transcript for possible 'consequences' (trend/APA). The same day the FPÖ announced it would extend the committee by three months, which it can do on its own. Stocker is not accused of any offence.
key_facts: 22 October 2025: inquiry committee set up (Parliament)
8 July 2026: summons of Stocker and others decided (PK0705/2026)
21 October 2026: Stocker testified as Auskunftsperson for about three hours (trend/APA)
21 October 2026: the FPÖ announced a three-month extension of the committee (trend/APA)

title: Wiener Neustadt: ÖVP–FPÖ cooperation in the city government (2015–2025)
description: In 2015 the ÖVP took over Wiener Neustadt, governed by the SPÖ for about 70 years, through a pact with the FPÖ presented as a 'colourful city government', in which the Greens also voted for ÖVP mayor Klaus Schneeberger; Stocker, the ÖVP's city leader, left the mayoralty to Schneeberger and remained vice-mayor (ORF, profil). profil described Stocker and FPÖ secretary-general Michael Schnedlitz as key figures of the pact, reported that, according to ÖVP official Matthias Zauner, no council decision since 2015 had been taken without joint support, and recalled that FPÖ city councillor Udo Landbauer's 2017 refusal to renew the permit of the 'Kebap-Ali' snack stand, backed by Mayor Schneeberger, caused nationwide outrage. The Green group leader in the city described the arrangement as a de facto ÖVP single-party government. The pact drew national attention in January 2025, when Stocker opened federal coalition talks with the FPÖ.
key_facts: 2015: ÖVP-led city government with FPÖ support; Schneeberger mayor, Stocker vice-mayor (ORF, profil)
profil (12 January 2025): Stocker and Schnedlitz described as key figures of the local ÖVP–FPÖ cooperation
2017: 'Kebap-Ali' permit dispute under FPÖ councillor Landbauer (profil)
